thread:
nina: Quick brain-dump — propose we ship a transient 'bridge adapter' (edge or sidecar) that translates legacy client v1 requests into the new v3 wire format so we can give customers more runway before forcing SDK upgrades. Thinking: opt-in feature flag, telemetry + circuit breaker, 12w deprecation notice. Thoughts?

samir: +1 in principle. two main choices: per-tenant sidecar (more control, lower global blast radius) vs single edge translator (easier to maintain ops-wise). Sidecar costs more infra.

eva: Edge translator will add latency for all tenants unless we shortcut by header sniffing. We should measure p95 delta. Also streaming and function-calls are tricky.

miguel: Streaming is the hard part — v1 used chunked SSE, v3 uses framed JSON streaming with explicit event types. The bridge must translate and preserve backpressure and connection timeouts. If we naively buffer, we'll blow memory.

nina: agree. Implementation constraints: keep translations stateless where possible, avoid buffering whole responses, and emit metrics for any translations that do buffering.

samir: For detection, simplest heuristic: X-Client-Version header or Accept header sniff. Example: 

```python
if req.headers.get('X-Client-Version') == 'v1':
    route_to_bridge()
else:
    pass_through()
```

That keeps perf cheap for modern clients.

eva: Also: token accounting. translated requests can inflate token count (extra envelope fields). We must surface "token_inflation_pct" in billing telemetry so customers don't get surprised.

miguel: We should implement a soft-fallback mode: if translation fails, return 426 Upgrade Required with a helpful body instructing client upgrade + a link to migration guide. But don't hard-block initially.

samir: Telemetry / alerts proposal: bridge.v1_requests (counter), bridge.v1_errors (counter), bridge.added_latency_ms (histogram), bridge.token_inflation_pct (gauge), bridge.streaming_drops (counter). Create an SLO for translation error rate < 0.5% and p95 added latency < 50ms for warm paths.

nina: rollout plan sketch:
- Week 0: internal canary (eng + se tenants) with sidecar deploys
- Week 2: opt-in TTL flag for selected customers, collect metrics
- Week 6: auto-opt-in for low-risk tenants with a clear undo toggle
- Week 12: deprecation announcement + provide migration tooling
- Week 20: scheduled enforce (only if metrics show low impact)

eva: Tests: must include streaming e2e harness and a fuzz runner for malformed v1 payloads. Add contract-suite against the oldest supported SDK.

miguel: One more: circuit-breaker config to avoid thundering herd when bridge flaps. Example: 

```yaml
circuit_breaker:
  max_failures: 5
  reset_interval: 30s
  half_open_requests: 3
```

samir: Good. Also add a header we set when translation happened so we can filter traces: X-Redwood-Translated: v1->v3. Makes debugging much easier.

nina: Ops checklist I'm going to add to the RFC follow-up doc:
- toggle flags for per-tenant opt-in/opt-out
- metrics and dashboards + default alert thresholds
- smoke tests and streaming harness in CI
- circuit-breaker + retry semantics documented
- migration docs + sample SDK snippets
- billing notice and token_inflation visibility

miguel: Should we build bridge as a short-lived library + config so Dedicated/Private customers can opt to run locally? Might be useful for regulated tenants who don't want us in the path.

eva: Yes — provide two artifacts: (1) hosted edge translation service we operate, (2) small sidecar binary (Go) with the same behavior that customers can run. Keep feature parity but prefer sidecar for Private deployments.

samir: I can own telemetry names + dashboard mockups. Will open a PR with suggested dashboards and alert rules.

nina: Great. @deploy-bot can you queue a tiny canary job for the prototype sidecar so we can test basic path? If possible run against streaming harness.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: canary-job-8142 — will run streaming + token-inflation smoke tests and post results to #ci-results when done.

nina: Perfect. I'll write the follow-up RFC and include the ops checklist and timeline. Thanks all — planning notes will go in the RFC doc, linking to the canary once results land. :+1:
